bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 67263 (gpac): Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_probe_analyze [asan].
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json.issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / staged `poc` bytes
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 1033-byte text file with SHA-256 `df782f9d3934a50dd9b85a935cbc7c63590a40a2a9aaf6bde147c8a80abcd45e`. GPAC first admits that file as an `application/x-gpac-playlist`, then `filelist_next_url()` reads its only non-comment line, which is the SAT>IP URL `satip://<1024-byte host>/`. `filelist_load_next()` forwards that line into source loading, probe dispatch selects the RTP input filter because the URL starts with `satip://`, and generic filter argument parsing stores the same string in `GF_RTPIn.src`. `rtpin_initialize()` takes its SAT>IP branch and calls `rtpin_satip_get_server_ip(ctx->src, ctx->session->satip_server)`. Inside that helper, `test = strstr(sURL, "://") + 3` points to a 1025-byte substring made of 1024 host bytes followed by the final `/`, and `len = strlen(test)` therefore becomes 1025. The loop at `src/filters/in_rtp.c:119-124` copies the 1024 host bytes into the local `text[1024]` array and breaks on the slash with `i == 1024`, but there is no bound that reserves room for the terminator in `text`. The next statement `text[i] = 0` at `src/filters/in_rtp.c:126` therefore writes one byte past the stack buffer, and Stage 01 reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at that line. The staged fix clamps this and the sibling terminator stores with `MIN(i, GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(text)-1)` so the witnessed `i == 1024` case no longer indexes past `text`.

source.description: First project-side read that materializes the attacker-controlled playlist line into the URL string later forwarded to source loading.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 1033-byte UTF-8 text file with SHA-256 `df782f9d3934a50dd9b85a935cbc7c63590a40a2a9aaf6bde147c8a80abcd45e`. Its only non-comment line is `satip://<1024-byte host>/`, and `filelist_probe_data()` accepts those bytes as a GPAC playlist before this `gf_fgets()` call reads that exact line into `szURL` on the crashing path.

root_cause.description: The server-name copy loop limits `i` only by the attacker-derived substring length and delimiter position, not by the 1024-byte `text` buffer. On the staged witness it exits with `i == 1024`, leaving no room for the terminator written immediately afterward.
root_cause.note: The staged fix addresses this witnessed obligation by clamping the subsequent `text[i] = 0` store to `GF_ARRAY_LENGTH(text)-1`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. After the loop has left `i == 1024`, this statement writes a NUL terminator to `text[1024]`, one byte past the 1024-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 1` at `src/filters/in_rtp.c:126:10` and identifies local `text` from line 74 as the overflowing stack object.

tainted_value_origin.description: This strips the `satip://` scheme and materializes the server substring that drives the later length calculation and copy loop. For the staged witness, `test` spans 1025 bytes: 1024 host bytes followed by `/`.

parser_admitted.description: The temporary file passes GPAC's playlist probe because it is legal UTF-8 without BOM and contains at least one non-comment line made only of URL characters. That is why the fuzz input reaches `filelist_next_url()` instead of being rejected earlier.

target_filter_selected.description: After `filelist_next_url()` extracts the URL line, source-probe dispatch admits that line to the RTP input filter because it starts with the `satip://` scheme.

coarse_trace.summary: GPAC admits the staged text file as a playlist, and `filelist_next_url()` reads the single attacker-controlled line `satip://<1024-byte host>/` into `szURL`.
FileList forwards that SAT>IP line into source loading, probe dispatch selects the RTP input filter for the `satip://` scheme, and source argument parsing stores the same string in `ctx->src`.
`rtpin_initialize()` takes the SAT>IP branch, and the helper derives `test = sURL + 8`, `len = 1025`, and a 1024-byte destination array `text` for the server name.
The helper copies the 1024 host bytes into `text[0..1023]`, leaves `i == 1024` when it breaks on the trailing slash, and then overflows the stack buffer by executing `text[1024] = 0`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `gf_fgets()` reads the only non-comment playlist line from the staged file into `szURL`. On the crashing witness that line is `satip://<1024-byte host>/`, so `szURL` now holds the attacker-controlled SAT>IP URL later handed to source loading.
`url` aliases the line read in step 1, and FileList forwards that SAT>IP string into GPAC's source-loader dispatch as the next source to open.

During source loading, the attacker URL is admitted to the RTP input filter specifically because it starts with `satip://`. `gf_fs_load_source_dest_internal()` uses this positive probe result to select `rtpin` for the new source.
After `rtpin` is selected, the generic source loader packages the chosen source as the explicit argument string `src=satip://<1024-byte host>/` for that filter instance.
Generic filter argument parsing interprets the `src=` string from step 4 using `RTPInArgs[0]`, so the RTP input instance's `ctx->src` field becomes the attacker URL before `rtpin_initialize()` runs.
With `ctx->src` starting `satip://`, initialization takes the SAT>IP branch, allocates `ctx->session->satip_server`, and calls `rtpin_satip_get_server_ip()` on the attacker URL.
Inside the helper, the local destination buffer `text` has fixed capacity 1024 bytes total, including any terminator copied or written later.
The helper strips the `satip://` prefix and sets `test` to the server substring. For the staged witness, `test` is 1025 bytes long: 1024 host bytes followed by the final `/` at offset 1024.
The attacker-derived server substring length becomes `len = 1025`, so the subsequent loop is willing to examine indices 0 through 1024 in `test`.

Starting from `i = 0`, the loop copies the 1024 host bytes into `text[0..1023]` and then breaks when `test[1024] == '/'`. Because the loop only checks `i < len` and delimiter position, it exits with `i == 1024` and no reserved room for `text`'s terminator.
With `i == 1024`, this terminator write targets `text[1024]`, one byte past the end of the stack buffer. AddressSanitizer reports the witnessed 1-byte stack-buffer-overflow here.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. This chain is closed from the staged vulnerable source, the saved AddressSanitizer run, the patch hunk, and the exact staged witness bytes only.

The staged patch also hardens a distinct `schema[10]` path and an earlier `text` terminator after port parsing, but the saved crash witnesses only the final server-name terminator write at `src/filters/in_rtp.c:126`; this GT traces that exact witnessed path only.

The saved stack does not include a specialized setter frame for `ctx->src`. The `ctx->src` binding in step 5 is grounded by the explicit `src=<sURL>` string built in `gf_fs_load_source_dest_internal`, the call to `gf_filter_parse_args()`, and the vulnerable-source `RTPInArgs[0]` mapping for `src`.

allocation_context.description: ASan's stack-frame report names local `text` declared at line 74 as the overflowing object and shows the bad write landing at offset 1088, exactly one byte past that 1024-byte array.

format.name: GPAC playlist text containing a SATIP URL
format.contract: The staged `poc` is the exact 1033-byte UTF-8 playlist text with SHA-256 `df782f9d3934a50dd9b85a935cbc7c63590a40a2a9aaf6bde147c8a80abcd45e`. It must be accepted by GPAC's playlist parser as a single non-comment source line `satip://<1024-byte host>/`, and that line must reach `rtpin_satip_get_server_ip()` unchanged so the substring after `://` is exactly 1024 host bytes followed immediately by `/`. This makes the copy loop stop with `i == 1024`, and the subsequent `text[i] = 0` write executes on `text[1024]`.
